+package main
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+)
+
+// Correctly simulating the original logic
+func originalLogic(idx, length int, isPut bool) bool {
+	// Note: Returning true means "out of bounds" (error condition)
+	return idx < 0 || (!isPut && idx >= length) || idx > length
+}
+
+func fixedLogic(idx, length int, isPut bool) bool {
+	// Clearer version of the same logic
+	return idx < 0 || idx > length || (idx == length && !isPut)
+}
+
+func main() {
+	testCases := []struct {
+		idx    int
+		length int
+		isPut  bool
+		desc   string
+	}{
+		{0, 5, false, "Valid: first element, not PUT"},
+		{4, 5, false, "Valid: last element, not PUT"},
+		{5, 5, false, "Invalid: beyond last element, not PUT"},
+		{5, 5, true, "Valid: append position, PUT"},
+		{-1, 5, false, "Invalid: negative index"},
+		{-1, 5, true, "Invalid: negative index, PUT"},
+		{6, 5, true, "Invalid: too far beyond, PUT"},
+		{6, 5, false, "Invalid: too far beyond, not PUT"},
+	}
+
+	fmt.Println("Testing original vs fixed logic:")
+	fmt.Println("Idx\tLen\tIsPut\tOrig\tFixed\tMatch\tDescription")
+	for _, tc := range testCases {
+		orig := originalLogic(tc.idx, tc.length, tc.isPut)
+		fixed := fixedLogic(tc.idx, tc.length, tc.isPut)
+		match := orig == fixed
+		fmt.Printf("%d\t%d\t%t\t%t\t%t\t%t\t%s\n", tc.idx, tc.length, tc.isPut, orig, fixed, match, tc.desc)
+	}
+}
